text:
David Pastrnak called the Bruins' start "unacceptable" in the middle of a winning run, and the numbers explain why he wasn't satisfied. Boston is 13-6-1 with 27 points, but it has allowed 10.5 fewer goals than its chances would usually produce. The process is decent, 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), not dominant.

The goaltending is doing a lot. Michael DiPietro is 4-0-0 with a .930 save percentage and 5.5 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. The Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy pair is the engine underneath: 64% of the chances and a 12-6 goal edge in more than 200 minutes. Pastrnak, Pavel Zacha and JJ Peterka have outscored teams 9-4.

The setback is James Hagens. The rookie is expected to miss a few weeks after the incident against Pittsburgh, and his line with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt had been winning its minutes, 8-3 in goals. Somebody has to fill that hole.

Then came a 6-2 loss to Minnesota, which has now outscored Boston 10-3 in two meetings. Our numbers put the playoff odds at 77%. What we'd watch: whether the goaltending keeps covering for a team that takes five penalties a game, and whether Pastrnak's warning turns into a better week.
